title: Hematemesis
chief_complaint: Hematemesis and melena in a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a 55-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis who presents with hematemesis and melena. He is found to have severe anemia (Hct 24%, Hgb 8.0 g/dL), mild coagulopathy (INR 1.8), and thrombocytopenia (platelets 100,000). Evaluate for upper GI bleeding from portal hypertension — esophageal varices are the leading concern.
case_summary:
Differential: Esophageal varices, peptic ulcer disease, Mallory-Weiss tear, gastric erosions, malignancy.

Esophageal varices are dilated submucosal veins that develop as a consequence of portal hypertension, most commonly from cirrhosis. This case presents a classic scenario: a 55-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis presenting with hematemesis and melena, found to have severe anemia (Hct 24%, Hgb 8.0), mild coagulopathy (INR 1.8), and thrombocytopenia (platelets 100,000).

The definitive diagnosis is made via urgent esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) with band ligation. Acute management: type and crossmatch, cautious IV resuscitation, restrictive PRBC transfusion (Hb 7–9 g/dL), octreotide IV, IV PPI, ceftriaxone prophylaxis in cirrhotics with GI bleed, and NPO for endoscopy. With platelets 100,000 and INR 1.8, platelet or FFP transfusion is NOT required. Spironolactone is contraindicated during acute variceal hemorrhage. After stabilization: non-selective beta-blocker for secondary prophylaxis, hepatitis A/B vaccination, alcohol cessation counseling, and lactulose to prevent hepatic encephalopathy.
case_introduction:
Case Introduction

Hematemesis — Emergency Medicine
A 55-year-old man with alcoholic cirrhosis presents with hematemesis and melena.
physical_exam: Ill-appearing; assess for shock, jaundice, cachexia, and stigmata of chronic liver disease.
Tachycardia; evaluate for hypotension indicating hypovolemia.
Evaluate for respiratory distress or aspiration.
Assess for ascites, splenomegaly, or tenderness suggesting portal hypertension.
Alert unless encephalopathy or perfusion compromise; watch for hepatic encephalopathy after bleed.

patient_voice.chief_complaint: I've been vomiting blood and my stools have been black. I'm terrified.
patient_voice.history: I have cirrhosis from alcohol. This started today — I threw up blood and noticed dark stools.
patient_voice.pain: My belly feels full and I'm weak and dizzy when I stand up.

stacks.finding: Prepare for possible transfusion in active bleeding.

stacks.finding: Diagnostic and therapeutic for variceal bleeding — most important intervention.

stacks.label: Saline solution, normal
stacks.finding: Volume resuscitation in hypovolemic shock; avoid over-resuscitation worsening portal pressure.

stacks.label: Transfusion, packed red blood cells
stacks.finding: If Hb ≤8 g/dL or ongoing bleeding, transfuse to maintain Hb >7 with restrictive strategy.

stacks.label: Octreotide acetate
stacks.finding: Vasoconstrictor reducing portal pressure and variceal bleeding.

stacks.label: Diet, NPO
stacks.finding: NPO to prepare for urgent endoscopy.
aliases: Nothing by mouth except ice chips

stacks.label: Pantoprazole sodium
stacks.finding: IV PPI to reduce rebleeding risk; IV route preferred over oral PPI in acute bleed.

stacks.label: Ceftriaxone sodium
stacks.finding: Prophylactic antibiotics in cirrhotic with GI bleed — prevents SBP and reduces mortality.

stacks.label: Vaccine, Hepatitis A, inactivated
stacks.finding: Prevent superinfection in chronic liver disease; recommended for all with cirrhosis.

stacks.label: Vaccine, hepatitis B
stacks.finding: Prevent superinfection in chronic liver disease; recommended for all with cirrhosis.

stacks.label: Advise patient, no alcohol
stacks.finding: Prevent progression of cirrhosis and recurrent bleeds.

stacks.finding: Non-selective beta-blocker for secondary prophylaxis after bleeding controlled — not during acute instability.

stacks.label: Instruct patient, smoking cessation
stacks.finding: Address modifiable risk factor during hospitalization.

stacks.label: Lactulose
stacks.finding: Prevent hepatic encephalopathy after upper GI bleed in cirrhosis.

decoys.label: Spironolactone
decoys.reason_wrong: Contraindicated during acute variceal hemorrhage — patient is volume-depleted; diuretic risks hypotension and AKI.

decoys.label: Omeprazole
decoys.reason_wrong: Oral PPI loses points — IV pantoprazole/esomeprazole preferred in acute upper GI bleed.

decoys.label: Levofloxacin
decoys.reason_wrong: Inferior prophylactic choice in cirrhotic GI bleed — ceftriaxone/cefotaxime preferred over quinolones.

decoys.label: Transfusion, platelets
decoys.reason_wrong: Platelets 100,000 — transfusion not indicated unless <50,000 with active bleeding.

decoys.label: Transfusion, fresh frozen plasma
decoys.reason_wrong: INR 1.8 without indication for FFP in this scenario — restrictive transfusion strategy applies.

decoys.label: Reproductive
decoys.reason_wrong: Male patient — pregnancy-related orders not indicated.
